items.text: stimulating; unexciting but likable. Sol.760.(c) Wander - to walk somewhere slowly with no particular sense of direction or purpose Amble to walk at a slow relaxed speed Bustle - to move in a busy, noisy, or exciting way Stare - to look at somebody or something for a long time because you are surprised, shocked, etc. Trot - to move forward at a speed that is faster than a walk Sol.761.(b) 'Slick' means clever at persuading people but perhaps not completely honest. The given sentence states that the university team won the match in the end with a slick(cunning) move. Hence, 'slick' is the most appropriate answer. Sol.762.(b) Agitated - feeling or appearing troubled or nervous. Initiated - to start something Animated - interesting and full of energy Triumphed - to achieve success Sol.763.(b) Serendipity - the fact of finding something valuable or interesting by accident or something pleasant happening by chance Godsend - something unexpected that is very useful because it comes just when it is needed Sibilance - a hissing quality of sound, or the hissing sound itself Catastrophe - a sudden disaster that causes great suffering or damage
